source.title: Unsupervised discovery of functional sequence patterns from protein language model with MotifAE
source.authors: Chao Hou; Di Liu; Yu-Feng Shen

page_placements.theme: Interpretable sparse dictionary features across model domains

record.file_problem: The full article text is present. It is marked Article in Press.
record.tranche_reason: The study applies sparse autoencoders to ESM2-650M protein-language-model embeddings and reports that the resulting features identify functional sequence patterns. This extends indirect evidence about sparse features recoverable from language-model representations to protein language models; it does not test toy-model superposition geometry.
record.gate_note: The study reports feature recovery and functional correspondence in a protein language model, not competition between more-than-dimensional sparse features, near-orthogonal directions, or a capacity account of polysemanticity. No rows are included for cited results from other studies. The paper also reports reconstruction and downstream prediction results, but those do not directly measure the claim versions. The feature-granularity findings do not establish whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical.
record.test_reason: The study uses a sparse autoencoder as a tool on ESM2-650M final-layer embeddings. Its results are its own method's performance (MotifAE vs a standard SAE) on motif and domain identification and fitness tasks. It does not ask whether the pLM stores features in superposition. It skips the controls (raw-embedding neurons, shuffled-weight pLM) that would separate model-held sparse features from SAE-imposed ones, citing a prior study. Sparsity (~46 active latents) was tuned by loss weights, so it is a design choice, not a finding. No version is tested; the feature-recovery results are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that MotifAE's smoothness loss markedly improves identification of known functional motifs over a standard SAE while preserving sparsity and reconstruction. They find its features show diverse sequence patterns reflected in decoder weight space, capture some domains, and correlate with residue importance. They also report that the supervised MotifAE-G extension identifies stability-associated features that help predict stability and guide redesign in silico.
record.recipe_differences: This study trains a sparse autoencoder with an added sequence smoothness loss on protein-language-model embeddings; it does not reproduce the original toy-network setup or its geometric measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports similar performance for smoothness window sizes of three, four, and five residues, and lower performance for domains with high contact order.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE latents trained on ESM2-650M final-layer embeddings recover ELM motifs (standard SAE median best-match AUROC 0.80; MotifAE 0.88) and CATH domains better than permuted activations. There is no control on raw neurons or a randomized model.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sparse dictionary features from protein language model embeddings align with annotated functional motifs and domains.

fits_no_version.finding: Motif–feature matches are many-to-many. 67 of 114 matched motifs match multiple features, and 55 of 146 features match multiple motifs, for example f27416 for C-terminal motifs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dictionary features vary in granularity relative to biological annotation categories.

record.problems: The evidence concerns one protein language model and does not measure feature geometry or test general-purpose LLMs. The paper reports that domain performance decreases at high contact order, and its CATH Others subset is small (n = 8) with a non-significant comparison. MotifAE features have varying granularity, including features associated with multiple motifs.

untested.parts: All; no toy models, interference, sparsity transition or geometry.
All; no capacity or importance analysis of neurons.
All; ESM2 neuron polysemanticity is not examined.
Whether ESM2 spreads features across neurons, or contains sparse features beyond what the SAE imposes. No neuron baseline or random-model control is run.
Completeness, stability across seeds or settings, and canonicity. Only granularity is noted, as many-to-many motif–feature matches.
All; dimensionality of features is not examined.

record.verdict_notes: Reclassified from T3/tests to T4/uses_without_test. This is an SAE-application method paper whose results are benchmarks of the study's own method; it does not test superposition. The authors explicitly omit raw-embedding and shuffled-weight controls, so feature recovery cannot be attributed to sparse features held by the model rather than to the dictionary. Nor is it compared against neuron-level polysemanticity. The reader's V4 labels are withdrawn.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, overcomplete sparse feature storage, interference, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether features compete for limited capacity or important features receive dedicated dimensions while others share.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise through mechanisms other than capacity pressure.

The study tests feature recovery in ESM2-650M, a protein language model, not a range of general-purpose LLMs; it does not quantify how individual features are distributed across ordinary model neurons.
Completeness, stability across training runs or settings, and canonical status of SAE features.
Whether represented features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional structures.

rows.subject: ESM2-650M (MotifAE feature f27416)

rows.value: C-terminal motifs: median AUROC 0.97 for 25 motifs; the feature matched 17 motifs, all located at protein C-termini

rows.note: The paper presents this as an example of features capturing shared or more general patterns, rather than one feature per specific motif.
rows.check: A single-feature example of a general C-terminal feature. The 'partial' state is not meaningful; the result is strong (median AUROC 0.97) but bears on feature granularity, not on a version.
